description: The episode prompt for the repetition pass on VIDEO input: one JSON object per episode, sent first in the user turn, followed by one video per camera in video_order (a head MP4 run sends the head video only). The model samples the video at context.step_interval_s (Gemini videoMetadata.fps = 1 / step_interval_s). Step n is the fixed sampling point at t_s = (n - 1) x step_interval_s from the start of the video; steps lists every step with its t_s. The steps are the fixed grid the model must answer in; it never builds its own step numbering, so code can map every step to a timestamp. The model converts what it sees at a video time to the nearest step and never outputs a time. Steps are sampling points, not every frame: the model should not assume actions between steps that the video does not show. No sensor timeline is included: the model counts repetitions from video only. The model identifies the task from the views provided and counts the cycles (repetitions) of that task in this episode.

context.rig: MCAP metadata recording.robot_type (umi_bimanual); 'UMI handheld rig' when unset
context.duration_s: episode length in seconds: recording.episode_length / video_fps (59.94)
context.step_interval_s: seconds between steps (= 1 / video sampling fps)
context.given_task: task text of the delivery order for this task folder (e.g. task01), when one was given; null when none. A hint, not a fact: the model describes what the video shows

views.head: head-mounted, forward facing: scene, object and destination locations, overall task progress
views.wrist_left: left gripper camera: left-hand grasp, contact, manipulation and release
views.wrist_right: right gripper camera: right-hand grasp, contact, manipulation and release
views.missing_views: video_order lists only the videos actually sent (head only for a head MP4); the model uses the remaining views and does not invent the missing ones
